source: DS14284 Rev 5 (STM32MP257x datasheet) cross-referenced with stm32mp251/255.dtsi and stm32mp257f-ev1.dts
notes: Clocks and regulators on STM32MP25 are virtualized through SCMI/OP-TEE: the kernel requests them from the secure world (scmi node), the real RCC/PWR/PMIC programming happens in TF-A. Disabling the secure clock/regulator providers bricks the boot just as surely as disabling RCC.
DDRCTRL/DDRPHY and STGEN are initialized by TF-A (BL2/BL31) and are NOT present as enabled nodes in the kernel DTS - they are mandatory firmware blocks, listed here for completeness.

The active boot-source peripheral depends on the BOOT0..BOOT3 pins + OTP. On the EV1 board the default is the SD card via SDMMC1; eMMC uses SDMMC2, serial NOR uses OCTOSPI (ommanager/ospi1). Exactly one boot source must be functional.

board_pin_locked.description: 這片板子實體已繞線、必須鎖回官方腳位 (must_bind) 的介面。腳位取自 baseline/signal_to_pin.json 的官方 pinout。此為『板級』設定：換別片板子這份清單會不同，與 LLM 輸入無關。solver 會把這些腳從其他訊號的候選域移除，確保不被搶走。

why.SDMMC1: micro-SD 卡槽（EV1 預設開機源）

pwr.why: Datasheet 3.9.1: the system requires supply on VDD, VDDA18AON, VDDCPU and VDDCORE to start; POR/PDR/BOR supervisors (3.9.2) hold the SoC in reset until thresholds are met.

rcc.why: Generates every clock and reset in the SoC (3.12). No RCC = no clock/reset to any IP, including the A35 that runs the boot code.

oscillators.why: Low-level boot starts on the internal HSI (~64 MHz), but major external interfaces (DDR, USB) require the external HSE crystal (3.12.1, p19). LSE/LSI feed RTC and the independent watchdog.
oscillators.dts_node: (clocks provided via rcc/scmi; crystals are board components)

ddr.block: DDRCTRL + DDRPHYC - DDR memory controller/PHY (with PLL2)
ddr.why: TF-A loads OP-TEE/U-Boot/OS into external DRAM; DDR init is mandatory for second-stage boot (3.7). Clocked by the dedicated PLL2, powered by VDDQDDR.
ddr.dts_node: (TF-A firmware device tree - not a kernel node)

sdmmc1.block: Boot source - SDMMC1 (default SD-card boot on EV1)
sdmmc1.why: The ROM code loads the FSBL from the boot source selected by BOOT0..3 + OTP (3.8). Exactly one boot interface must work; EV1 defaults to the micro-SD on SDMMC1 (eMMC -> SDMMC2, serial NOR -> OCTOSPI).

bsec.why: Holds the boot-mode and security configuration OTP read by the ROM code; reserved to the boot/trusted CPU (3.47). Powered from VDDA18AON.

stgen.block: STGEN - system time generator (A35 generic-timer base)
stgen.why: Provides the 64-bit time base for all Cortex-A35 generic timers; initialized early by TF-A (3.49 / 3.48.8). Without it the A35 timer/scheduler does not advance.

intc.why: The Cortex-A35 cluster interrupt controller (3.1.2.9); configured by TF-A. No GIC = no interrupts for the boot software.

rifsc.why: TF-A/OP-TEE must program RIFSC to grant the boot software access to peripherals; an unconfigured RIF leaves IPs inaccessible (3.11). Most peripheral nodes sit on the rifsc bus in the DTS.

risaf.block: RISAF - resource isolation for memory (DDR/memory firewall)
risaf.why: Guards DRAM and memory regions; TF-A configures RISAF so the boot stages and OS can access DDR (3.11). Includes on-the-fly DDR encryption (DDRMCE).

syscfg.why: System/pin/SRAM and interconnect configuration used during early boot (block diagram p12, RIF list p21).

tamp.why: Backup registers in the VSW/VBAT domain carry boot/secure state across reset; the boot chain reads/writes them (3.51). Anti-tamper inputs are optional.

scmi.block: SCMI / OP-TEE secure clock & regulator provider
scmi.why: On STM32MP25 the kernel obtains clocks and regulators (incl. CPU/DDR rails, ultimately the external PMIC e.g. STPMIC2) through SCMI to the secure world. If the secure provider is absent the kernel cannot bring up any clocked peripheral.

usart2.why: Not required for the SoC to boot, but it is the EV1 default serial console; without it the boot proceeds blind (no log/recovery).
